sentences.text: The claimant aggrieved by the inadequate compensation awarded by the learned Senior Civil Judge and JMFC, Bilagi, in LAC No.11/2011 dated 25.04.2017 has preferred this appeal seeking enhancement of compensation.
2. The land of the appellant has been acquired for Upper Krishna Project.
The Land Acquisition Officer has fixed the market value of the acquired land in a sum of Rs.84,973/- per acre.
The Reference Court has fixed the market value of the acquired land in a sum of Rs.3,25,000/- per acre.
The land of the claimant that is acquired is an irrigated land bearing Sy.No.56/1C measuring 1 acre 36 guntas.
Aggrieved by the award of inadequate compensation, the claimant has preferred this appeal.
Heard the learned counsel for the appellant and the learned High Court Government Pleader for the respondents.

4. Learned counsel for the appellant would contend that the price of sugarcane per ton is Rs.1,918.68 for the relevant year 2008-09 and without taking that into consideration, the Reference Court has erred in taking the average of sugarcane crop at Rs.1,300/- per ton.
On that point, the learned counsel for the appellant has placed reliance on the decision of the Division Bench of this Court rendered in MFA No.435/2005 and connected matters decided on 08.01.2008.

sentences.text: Learned High Court Government Pleader would contend that the Reference Court has rightly taken the average of preceding 3 years and rightly taken the average price of sugarcane per ton in a sum of Rs.1,300/- and awarded the compensation NC: 2024:KHC-D:11659 and fixed market value at Rs.3,25,000/- per acre.
With this, she prayed to dismiss the appeal.
6. Having heard the learned counsel, the Court has perused the material placed on record.

7. It is clear from Exs.P-27 to 29-the pricelist during the relevant year, that the price of sugarcane was Rs.1,918.68 per ton but the learned Reference Judge took the price at Rs.1,300/- per ton which is average price for 3 preceding years and not the exact price for the relevant year.
The Division Bench of this Court in the matter referred supra, has taken the exact price for the relevant year and calculated the market value based on the price of the sugarcane.

Considering the said aspect, the price of sugarcane for the relevant period i.e. 2008- 2009 at Rs.1,918.68 (rounded to Rs.1,900/-)
per ton yield of sugarcane is taken into consideration.

Therefore, the appellant/claimant is entitled to market value to be determined by taking yield per NC: 2024:KHC-D:11659 acre of sugarcane as 50 tons and per ton price at Rs.1,900/- along with all statutory benefits thereof

If the yield of 50 tons per acre and the price at Rs.1,900/- per ton of sugarcane is taken, the market value of the land under acquisition comes to Rs.4,75,000/- per acre by adopting multiplication method as has been done by the Reference Judge as against Rs.3,25,000/- as awarded by the Reference Court.

8. In view of the above, the appellant/claimant is entitled to compensation by determining the market value of the land under acquisition at the rate of Rs.4,75,000/- per acre with all statutory benefits less the amount of compensation which they have already received.
9. In the result, the appeal is partly allowed with costs.
The market value of the land acquired is fixed at Rs.4,75,000/- per acre.

The appellant/claimant is entitled to compensation at the NC:
2024:KHC-D:11659 rate of Rs.4,75,000/- per acre with all statutory benefits.

Sd/-
